summary:
plan.md is written. It rebuilds the hillside from the GROUND map (rising from y 1 in the north-east to y 63 in the south-east) and sets six rounded sandstone boulders up to 18 tall at x 34..76, z 46..71: tan with orange stains, tuff bases, mossy crowns, gaps and one leaning pair.
In front of the rocks, a dark-oak and spruce viewing deck (top y 37, x 42..66, z 30..45) juts out as a stepped prow toward the north-west on tall posts, with stone-brick trails up from the north and on to the south-east.
Warm lanterns, three trees kept to the east and south edges, and nothing tall in the north-west keep the city view open; no building or roof. The toolkit doesn't know the block name `chain`, so railings are fences. An open hillside from the GROUND map, with six rounded sandstone boulders, a dark-oak and spruce viewing deck jutting north-west, and stone-brick trails.
Warm lantern posts, moss and azaleas, and three trees only at the east and south edges keep the view open.
elements.md and plan.md (PALETTE, VOCABULARY, ROOMS, PARTS, NOTES) are written. All ids checked.

hillside terrain: parts/terrain.mjs interpolates the GROUND map bilinearly between cell centres, so centres are exact and the surface steps 1 block at a time. It calls hillCell on all 106x101 columns, with the mossy rock-foot ring, podzol under the trees and stone/andesite on steep cells. make.sh gives a whole build.nbt (352k blocks placed by this part, no refusals); I did not run mcd check or fit, and I did not render or look at it.
polish: Not run: mcd check, mcd fit and a render of the terrain.
I did not verify that the build's highest ground is y 63 or that the west knoll flanks come out as stone/andesite.
Reserved trail columns are left empty for trails.mjs; the trail part must fill them down to y 0 (trailRun fills dirt and stone below).

waste.what: Wrote the bilinear interpolation, the rise calculation and the rock-foot and tree masks by hand.
waste.tool: A vocab helper such as hillsideFromGrid(g, GROUND) that does the interpolation, rise and nearRock/podzol masks

companions.task: Hand-patch the surface material mix and the steep west-knoll flanks after viewing a render.

summary:
six giant rocks: parts/rocks.mjs builds R1..R6 as boulders (over: true), 14 tuff-lined cracks on N/W faces, brown_terracotta seams on R3 and R5, and R5 leaning 2 onto R2 (R2 leans 1).
make.sh runs whole (build.nbt 369,508 blocks); check shows 0 floating, 0 unsupported, 0 orphans after clearing 4 lean strays on R5's crown.
Rock writes into terrain cells are refused by runParts (2027 refused, all buried base cells), so the bases sit on the hillside, and rock courses under a higher hill column are clipped.
polish: 2027 rock writes refused by runParts because they fall in terrain cells (buried bases). The plan's 'overwrite its columns' note conflicts with the lock; the rocks sit on the hill, and courses below a higher column are clipped. Needs a decision in plan Notes or a terrain carve-out.
The boulder helper's domed crowns read as drums at the render scale (front-left and zoom tiles); the crown dome is not visible at this size. Helper-level issue, not fixed here.
R2 lean is approximated as lean 1 (the boulder helper shifts north-west, not purely west). R5's contact with R2's crown (x55..58, z57..60, y49..50) was not verified in the render.
No cleanup of refused cells was attempted; a tool that reports only refusals above the ground surface would tell whether any visible rock cell was lost.

waste.what: Found the lean strays (4 crown blocks over air) by reading check output, then hand-wrote their coordinates into a clear list.
waste.tool: A boulder option or a post-pass helper that removes unsupported crown blocks after lean, e.g. boulder(..., { lean, trimUnsupported: true }) or a check --fix that reports cells to clear.

waste.what: Worked out refused-write locations by reading parts-report.json (only first 8 refusedAt shown) instead of knowing which refusals were above the surface.
waste.cost: 1 report read, no way to know visible vs buried refusals
waste.tool: parts-report.json with a split of refusals above and below the terrain surface, or a per-part 'refused above ground' count.

waste.what: Checked the rock shapes by eye in the render (front-left, right elevation, zoom) to judge the dome and seam.
waste.tool: mcd render with a --crop box and a shape-profile readout (per-course radius) for a boulder, so the dome can be checked numerically.

companions.task: Shape the boulders by hand: domed crowns, bedding seams, and the R5 lean onto R2's crown. Give them the boulder course radii and the R2/R5 contact box to check.
Settle the buried-base conflict with the terrain part: decide whether rock cells under the hill surface should overwrite it, and where the surface must be cut for the rock bases.

summary:
viewing platform: Viewing platform built in parts/platform.mjs: stepped spruce deck at y37 with dark oak edge board, dark oak fascia and stripped joists at y36, 23 deckPost footings and posts (dark oak knee braces at three north posts), spruce rail with the plan's openings, two spruce benches, and hanging lanterns at (46,35,30) and (52,35,30).
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt. The platform placed 876 blocks with no refused writes and no off-palette blocks. check shows 0 floating and 0 orphans; fit is OK.
Zoomed north view shows the stepped prow on its posts, pads and rail as intended. Dusk lighting and the south view were not checked (rocks not built yet).
polish: Deck-corner lamp posts from LANTERN_POSTS at (42,30), (56,30), (66,38), (42,45), (66,45) sit on the deck footprint: the trails part must drop them. Rail corner lanterns at (42,30), (56,30), (66,38) are already placed by deckRail.
Deck-corner lanterns at (42,45) and (66,45) are not placed (back edge has no rail; (66,45) is an opening). Part 4 / dusk pass should decide whether to add them on a dark oak fence.
Post at (46,30) moved to (46,31) so the hanging lantern keeps its cell; recorded in plan.md Notes.
Rail has one-cell diagonal gaps at the notch corners (56,33)-(57,34) and (62,37)-(63,38): cosmetic, fence states only join edge neighbours.
Pads at (42,45) and the back posts may touch R1; the rocks part should confirm the deck back edge still reads as tucked against the rock.

Joists sit at even x only and posts stand on the 4-cell grid, so the south/east cantilever is unsupported by posts (structure check passes because logs connect to fascia). Needs a look against the concept before final sign-off.
Dusk light coverage on the deck not verified: the dusk pass must confirm every deck cell is within 6 of a lantern (currently 3 hanging/rail lanterns plus 3 rail corners).

waste.what: Worked out each deck cell's footprint, perimeter, post grid and brace side by hand from the PRONGS boxes.
waste.cost: about 15 minutes of reasoning plus 3 rebuilds
waste.tool: a deckFloor(g, prongs, {joists, posts, grid}) helper in vocab/h2 that lays fascia, joists, edge board and the deck, and returns the perimeter list for deckRail.

waste.what: Ordered the rail's perimeter path by hand (angle sort, then dropping the back edge and openings) and checked the fence and lantern output cell by cell.
waste.tool: deckRail accepting a footprint and an open-edge spec, and deriving its own ordered path.

waste.what: Found the knee braces were orphans (placed outside the deck at z 29, touching only the post) and moved them inside under the fascia. Found the post at (46,30) collided with the hanging lantern.
waste.cost: 2 retries; each needed a full make.sh and check
waste.tool: deckPost's brace option that checks for a fascia or joist above and picks the inside side automatically; a plan-conflict check that flags a post or pad on a lantern cell before the build.

waste.what: Checked whether deckPost pads fell on reserved trail columns (x 67) by reading the plan, not the tool.
waste.tool: a reserved-cell check in make.sh (writes into TRAIL cells from an earlier part flagged), or a list of reserved cells in the palette report.

companions.task: Place the deck-corner and back-edge lanterns and confirm every deck cell is within 6 of a light, using mcd light on the platform cells, instead of me counting by hand.
Lay the stone-brick footings on the steep hillside so the pads meet the rock and the ground cleanly at the back edge, next to R1.
Check the knee braces and the rail's diagonal notch corners so the fences and stairs join the way a real joiner would.

summary:
trails, sign and lamps: parts/trails.mjs builds the continuous stone-step trail (lower x67..68 from the north edge, east along z42..43, south along x78..79, stepped diagonal to (96..97,100)), the cleft spur (x60..61, z46..59), the trail sign at (69,41) and 11 lantern posts. Trail y follows the GROUND map at ground+1 with at most 1 block of rise per point.
make.sh writes a whole build.nbt: trails part 9636 blocks, 0 refused, 0 off-palette; mcd check shows no floating or unsupported blocks; mcd fit OK; zoom renders read as a stone staircase climbing the hill.
Posts moved off the trail: (79,52)→(80,52), (79,64)→(80,64), (94,96)→(90,96); the spur lantern stands at (59,59). Extra ground lanterns at (71,40), (81,58), (65,4).
polish: Landings: no flat stone-brick landing every 6-8 steps; the lower and upper trails are pure stair runs, with flats only where the ground flattens.
Spur starts flush with the deck top at y 37 and climbs to 43, not the plan's 38..44 (noted in plan.md Notes).
Lantern-post checklist item is only partly ticked: the five deck-corner lanterns and the two hanging lanterns belong to the platform part, and the plan's (61,58) spur post moved to (59,59).

Light coverage not measured: mcd light was not run on the trail, so the 9-cell ground-lantern spacing is by eye only; the trail edges from z 44 to 60 and the lower trail from z 31 to 43 may have gaps.
Trail edge borders (coarse_dirt/rooted_dirt) come from the terrain part's hillCell edge rule; not verified in this part's render.

waste.what: Worked out each trail column's ground height by hand from the GROUND map (counting values by index for col 22 and similar) before writing the generator.
waste.cost: about 10 minutes of counting and some wrong reads of the table
waste.tool: a `groundColumn(c)` / `groundAt(x,z)` export in vocab/base.mjs, so a part reads the terrain at any cell without counting by hand

waste.what: Found lamp posts on the trail (79,52),(79,64) and an unbuildable post at (94,96) only by trying each one; lampPost returns 0 on refusal and nothing says why.
waste.cost: 3 rebuilds and a per-post block scan of the saved nbt
waste.tool: lampPost (and the other h1/h2 helpers) should return {placed, refused:reason} and a `vocab/base.mjs` onTrail check that matches the diagonal band the plan actually lays, so posts are checked before they are placed

waste.what: Verified each lantern by scanning the saved build.nbt cell by cell with a one-off node script.
waste.tool: `mcd info` or `mcd check` listing lantern and sign positions per part, or a report line in parts-report.json for refused helper calls

waste.what: Trail landings and step heights are not in any helper: a staircase of 1-block rises with a flat every 6-8 steps had to be left out because trailRun takes raw points with no landing rule.
waste.cost: not implemented, about 1 extra hour of design time saved if the helper did it
waste.tool: a trailRun option `landingEvery: 7` that inserts a flat point, plus a `trailProfile(groundFn, cells)` helper that returns the y list for a path

companions.task: lay the trail's flat landings every 6-8 steps and the half-step slabs where the ground's rise is under a block, so the ramp steps evenly
check every stretch of trail and the spur is within about 9 cells of a light with mcd light, and place the ground lanterns where it is not
settle the coarse_dirt and rooted_dirt borders beside the trail and the spur, since the terrain part owns those cells but the trail sets their look

summary:
planting and trees: parts/planting.mjs is written and make.sh produces a whole build.nbt (363,710 blocks). Trees T1 (oak), T2 (jungle) and T3 (oak) stand on the terrain's podzol, with crowns of persistent leaves, and read as trees in the render.
Shrub clumps (azalea, flowering azalea, fern, large fern, short grass, moss carpet) are sampled 2-3 cells outside rock boxes and trail edges, clear of the deck, lamp posts, sign and benches. A local trimStrays pass removes stray crown leaves, so check reports 0 orphans and fit is OK.
Planting reports 801 placed, 0 refused and 0 off-palette. plan.md step 5 and the two elements.md items are ticked, with a note added to plan NOTES.
polish: After the merge, check that the shrub clumps sit at the rock feet and along the trail edges (they were scattered on the open slope in this copy because the rock and trail parts are stubs here), and that the merge reports 0 refusals for planting.
Tree T1 (98,44) and T2 (88,93) crowns must stay clear of any later part's blocks; re-run check after merge.

waste.what: Shrub spot selection: I scanned all 10k plot cells by hand-written Chebyshev-distance tests against every rock, trail, deck, post and bench box, plus a neighbourhood check on the trail.
waste.cost: about 60 lines of geometry code and one full-plot scan per rebuild; the first pass also needed a tuning round
waste.tool: a vocab helper such as `scatter(g, { near: box, ring: [2, 3], clearOf: [...], p, kinds })` that returns clear spots, so every planting part reuses it instead of re-deriving the ring test

waste.what: Tree orphan cleanup: I wrote a face-contact pass to remove crown leaves with at most one solid neighbour, because the fit check flagged 8 orphan leaves on the first build.
waste.cost: one failed check, a rebuild, and about 25 lines of code
waste.tool: `tree()` in h1 should trim its own strays (leaves with at most one solid face) before returning, so `mcd check` never reports orphans from a tree

waste.what: Verification by eye: I could only judge the trees from the full-plot render. The shrubs look scattered across the open slope because the rock and trail parts are still stubs in this copy, so I could not confirm they cluster at the rock feet and trail edges.
waste.cost: one full render (about 10 s) and a visual check that could not confirm the shrub placement
waste.tool: a close-up `mcd zoom --at` on the rock feet and the trail once the merged build exists, or a `mcd render --closeups` tile around each plant site

companions.task: Check the rock-foot line: the boulders are ellipses inside their boxes, so the true base is narrower than the box, and the shrub spots at 2-3 cells outside should be re-measured against the built rocks after merge.
Confirm the trail border cells (coarse dirt and rooted dirt, one cell each side) against the planting spots, so no clump lands on a border cell that the trail part wants to own.
Review the crown shapes of T1 to T3 (the jitter and the trimmed strays) so they read as irregular broadleaf crowns from the hero view rather than as spheres.

summary:
dusk light pass: parts/dusk.mjs is built and runs last: it reads the lanterns and trail already in g, and adds deck lamp posts (dark_oak_fence with a lantern on top) and trail lamp posts only where a walkable cell is out of reach. It also reports cells above y 74 or outside the plot (0 in the current make.sh build).
On a stand-in deck and lower trail (platform and trails are stubs in this copy), all 385 deck cells reached light 9+ with 15 lamp posts, and the lower trail reached min 6 with 9 posts; `mcd fit` is OK on both.
make.sh produces a whole build.nbt (362,909 blocks, no refused or off-palette writes in the dusk line). plan.md item 6 and the elements dusk item are ticked, with a note that the check was on stand-ins.
polish: Not yet checked on the merged build: the deck and trail coverage was checked only on stand-ins (the platform and trail parts are stubs in this copy). Recheck `mcd light build.nbt --rooms ...` for the deck and the trail after the merge.
The lower trail's north end still has 2 cells at light 1-7 on the stand-in (no lamp site fit). The merged trail may differ.

Deck lamps: 15 posts, all deck cells at light 9+. The plan's 'within 6' gives light 9; light 8 (within 7) would need fewer posts. Kept 6 to match elements.md, which the plan wins over the lamplighter's 8+ rule. Worth a look at the render, since 15 posts is a lot for the deck.

Scope: the open hillside outside the deck and trail is not lit by this pass. The spec's 'light every roof and terrace' has no roofs here; the rock crowns and open ground are not covered, so mobs can spawn there.

waste.what: Light coverage was worked out by my own Manhattan estimate in dusk.mjs, then checked afterwards with `mcd light` on a stand-in file. I had no way to see the real light map while the pass was still placing lamps.
waste.cost: About 4 debug rounds: a wrong score (reach 8 instead of 7 with the lantern height counted), the trail sited on unbuilt reserved columns, and the border cells missed. Each round was a full make.sh.
waste.tool: A build-library helper such as `coverLights(g, cells, {reach, from})` that returns the uncovered cells and the best lamp site, using the same block-light spread as `mcd light`. Then the lamplighter needs no estimate of its own.

waste.what: I wrote a temporary stand-in harness (terrain, a deck top and a lower trail via trailRun, then the dusk pass) to test the pass when the other parts are stubs. It was deleted afterwards.
waste.cost: One file, about 15 lines, plus a `/tmp` rooms file per room.
waste.tool: `mcd light` could take a room box in the build being run (`--rooms` inside the build), and `runParts` could take a `--only <part>` option, so a part can be tested alone against the earlier parts.

waste.what: Reading the lantern list and the trail columns by scanning g.cells, and the per-iteration lantern rescans, were done in plain JS.
waste.cost: Negligible run time, but the scans repeat for each lamp added.
waste.tool: A `g.findBlocks(pattern)` or `g.lanterns()` query on the Grid.

companions.task: Pick where the trail and deck lamp posts go so they read as placed and keep the walkway clear, and check the lamp spacing against the trail's stair rhythm.
Fit the deck lamp posts into the rail and bench layout, so each one sits inside the railing without blocking the bench fronts or the trail exit.

summary: inspection: walk ok and fit OK, nothing to fix
